chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Kufi, from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Tahhan, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying:
There are five fruits of Paradise in this world: the Amlesi pomegranate, apples, quince, grapes, and ripe dates (mushan).
ai.seo_question: What are the five fruits of Paradise mentioned in this world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to illustrate the concept of *tashbih* (likeness) between the material and spiritual realms, suggesting that these five fruits—pomegranate, apple, quince, grape, and fresh dates—serve as earthly prototypes of celestial delights. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of finding divine signs in nature, reinforcing the idea that the physical world is a mirror of the hereafter.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-48 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Suleiman al-Kufy, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Tahan, on the authority of someone who quoted Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
There are five heavenly fruits in this world. They are pomegranates, apples, quince, grapes, and ripe dates.”
